newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA SAYS MARGINS TO TEST 97/98 PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: CBA SAYS MARGINS TO TEST 97/98 PROFITS.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia managing director David Murray said on Wednesday that lower home loan margins, further capital expenditure and higher labour costs will test profitability in the year to June 30, 1998.
"We have said it will be testy for a number of reasons. The hangover effect of reduction of home loan margins,...we still have unit labour costs rising," Murray told reporters.

"We will be making further investments in our financial services integration which will reflect on operating margins. So taken overall with a modest upkick in bad debts in the coming year we will see margin pressure," he said.

The bank earlier reported a fall in net profit to A$1.078 billion in the year to June 30 from A$1.119 billion in 1995/96, with the latest period including an abnormal loss of A$200 million from technology restructuring costs.
